lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! This one is about realms.
Two CI jobs on one machine, and both want a cluster called default? Without realms, they'd collide on the same names.
A realm is a namespace for everything sind creates: the mesh, DNS, SSH, and every cluster.
Its name goes in front of every resource. The default realm is called sind, so you get names like sind mesh.
Another realm gets its own copies, and even its own lock. Realms never wait for each other, and can't see each other at all.
Here, the dev and staging realms each create a cluster called app, side by side, with no conflict.
And each one is deleted on its own, without touching the other.
sind picks the realm in this order: first the realm flag, then the sind realm environment variable.
Next, a realm in the configuration file, which only sind create cluster reads. And last, the default, sind.
That third one has a catch. Here, the configuration file sets a realm of its own.
The commands that follow don't read that file, so pass them the same realm, or they look in another one.
So: one realm per parallel job, passed to every command, and no waiting on another realm's lock.
Next up: the cluster lifecycle. See you there!
